<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:5:3">Ib.</cite> <he>הא צ׳ … צְלוֹתָךְ</he> this is a prayer; now, may thy prayer be heard.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9:10">Y. Meg. I, 71ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>הדא … צריכה צ׳</he> this thy Torah scroll needs prayer (that it may not be condemned).
<cite ref="Yoma 28b:3">Yoma 28ᵇ</cite> <he>צְלוֹתֵיה דאברהם</he> the prayer time of Abraham (the afternoon prayer).

<cite ref="Berakhot 26a:17">Ber. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>כיון דצ׳ רחמי היא וכ׳</he> since prayer is a matter of love (contrad. to sacrifice), one may pray whenever one desires; a. fr.—Pl. <he>צַלְוָון</he>, <cite ref="R00516"><he>צַלְיָין</he></cite>. Targ. II Esth. V, 1 <he>שמע צליין</he> O hearer of prayers!—
Gen. R. s. 26 תרתיהון צ׳ אינון (not צלוונן) both of my wishes are prayers (and not curses); Yalk. ib. 43 צליין.—צְלוֹתַיָּא hymns.
